title: Entity

validation.research: Evans's accessible original DDD Reference, Entities on printed page 11, establishes continuing identity across lifecycle, changed attributes, and distinct representations. Fowler's Evans Classification establishes the reference-object alias, distinguishes value objects, and warns about overloaded database terminology; the example's identity-based operator is explicitly an implementation choice. Microsoft supports context-specific identity representations and behavior-bearing domain objects. Fowler's Identity Map catalog supports controlling duplicate loaded objects within a unit of work without implying global synchronization. Official Python documentation supports runtime identity, unsupported comparison results, hash obligations, frozen records, and underscore privacy limits. The equipment scenario, scoped key, equality policy, code, and illustrations are original teaching material.
validation.python_examples: Both actual article blocks execute and produce the four stated lines: recreated: True False; identity equal, labels equal: True False; same label, same entity: True False; other catalog: False. Checks pass for no model I/O imports, strict nonblank trimmed identifier fields, opaque text numbers including distinct 0042 and 42, case-sensitive catalog scope, frozen key fields, required typed identity, validated and normalized labels, read-only public properties, unchanged identity during multiple renames, unchanged state on invalid renames, stable hash and lookup by EquipmentId, explicitly unhashable Equipment, NotImplemented for unsupported comparisons, distinct concrete types, symmetric same-key equality, identical labels with distinct identities, independent objects with diverging state, preserved JSON snapshots, and reconstruction with an equal key in a different key and entity instance. Separate objects intentionally sharing a key also verify that this implementation supplies no allocation uniqueness or automatic synchronization.

example_limits: A single-threaded in-memory Equipment model with externally assigned catalog-local numbers, a frozen EquipmentId value, explicit concrete-type-and-key equality, unhashable mutable entities, and validated label changes. Public API conventions do not prevent deliberate underscore-field bypass. The JSON round trip is not a database or durable commit. Identifier allocation, persistent uniqueness, optimistic versions, locks, authorization, reconciliation, and automatic synchronization are not implemented. Equal identities deliberately do not imply equal or current state; this is not a universal operator policy for every Entity design.
publication: Local implementation only. No publishing, deployment, push, or pull request.
